title: Conjecture 5.3 of [24] (Induced Arithmetic Removal Lemma)
statement_text: An induced arithmetic removal lemma holds in general: for a fixed finite collection of $r$-colored arithmetic patterns, every coloring with $o(1)$ density of each such pattern can be recolored on an $o(1)$-fraction of the ambient space so that no such pattern remains.
context_text: The paper identifies this as a natural common extension of both the induced graph removal lemma and the arithmetic removal lemma. It is noted as not currently known, with [24, Conjecture 5.3] cited as one explicit formulation. The technique of deducing arithmetic removal from graph removal does not appear to extend to the induced setting.
paper_contribution: Proves the conjecture for complexity 1 patterns over finite fields $\mathbb{F}_q$: for every $\epsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta > 0$ such that if $\phi : V \setminus \{0\} \to [r]$ has $H$-density at most $\delta$ for every $H \in \mathcal{H}$, then there is a recoloring $\phi'$ that is $\mathcal{H}$-free and differs from $\phi$ on at most $\epsilon|V|$ elements (Theorem 1.14).

title: Open Problem (Extending Induced Arithmetic Removal to Higher Complexity and General Groups)
statement_text: Extend the induced arithmetic removal lemma beyond complexity 1 patterns over finite fields to higher complexity patterns and to general abelian groups (even the case of $\mathbb{Z}$ is open).
context_text: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and $V$ a finite-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-vector space. An $r$-colored pattern $H=(A,\psi)$ is an $\ell\times k$ matrix $A$ over $\mathbb{F}_q$ together with a coloring $\psi:[k]\to[r]$ of its columns; for a coloring $\phi:V\to[r]$, an $H$-instance is a tuple $(x_1,\dots,x_k)\in V^k$ with $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$ and $\phi(x_i)=\psi(i)$ for all $i$, the $H$-density is the number of $H$-instances divided by $|V|^{k-\mathrm{rank}A}$, and $\phi$ is $H$-free if there is no $H$-instance in $(V\setminus\{0\})^k$ (zero is ignored, since e.g. the solution $x=y=z=0$ of $x+y+z=0$ cannot be removed by recoloring). For functions $f_1,\dots,f_k:V\to\mathbb{C}$ let $\Lambda_A(f_1,\dots,f_k)$ be the average of $f_1(x_1)\cdots f_k(x_k)$ over all $\mathbf{x}\in V^k$ with $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$, and let $\widehat f(\gamma)$ denote the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at a character $\gamma$ of $V$. The matrix $A$ has complexity 1 if for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that for every $V$ and all $f_1,\dots,f_k:V\to[-1,1]$, $|\Lambda_A(f_1,\dots,f_k)|\le\epsilon$ whenever $\min_i\|\widehat f_i\|_\infty\le\delta$; examples are any single equation with at least three nonzero coefficients, or 3-term progressions, whereas 4-term progressions have complexity 2 (complexity $s$ means control by the Gowers $U^{s+1}$ norm, after Green and Tao). The authors prove the induced arithmetic removal lemma for complexity 1 patterns over finite fields: for a finite set $\mathcal{H}$ of $r$-colored complexity 1 patterns over $\mathbb{F}_q$ and every $\epsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that, for every $V$, if a coloring $\phi:V\to[r]$ has $H$-density at most $\delta$ for every $H\in\mathcal{H}$, then there is a recoloring $\phi':V\setminus\{0\}\to[r]$ that is $H$-free for all $H\in\mathcal{H}$ and differs from $\phi$ on at most $\epsilon|V|$ elements. This is an arithmetic analogue of the induced graph removal lemma of Alon, Fischer, Krivelevich and Szegedy (patterns of colors play the role of induced subgraphs), extending earlier work over $\mathbb{F}_2$ via a new recoloring technique. The authors state that extending this lemma to higher complexity patterns and to general abelian groups remains open (even over $\mathbb{Z}$). For affine-invariant patterns, a special case avoiding the difficulty of regularization near the origin, the problem for bounded complexity patterns over finite fields has been solved by Bhattacharyya, Fischer, Hatami, Hatami and Lovett. This is a problem of additive combinatorics.

title: Informal Conjecture (Induced Arithmetic Removal for Arbitrary Abelian Groups)
statement_text: A statement analogous to the induced arithmetic removal lemma for complexity 1 patterns over finite fields (a coloring with small density of every pattern of a fixed finite family can be made free of all of them by recoloring few elements) holds for arbitrary patterns (with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}$) in arbitrary abelian groups, subject to appropriate caveats concerning infinite complexity patterns and trivial solutions.
context_text: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and $V$ a finite-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-vector space. The authors conjecture that a similar statement holds for arbitrary patterns with integer coefficients in arbitrary abelian groups, but do not state a precise conjecture, because caveats are needed: in $\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z}$ colored red on $1,\dots,\lfloor N/2\rfloor$ and blue elsewhere, the pattern $x=y+1$ with $x$ blue and $y$ red has a single instance but cannot be removed by recoloring fewer than $\lfloor N/2\rfloor$ elements (this pattern has infinite complexity), and some trivial solutions, such as zero, must be ignored. This is a problem of additive combinatorics.

title: Informal Conjecture (Polynomial Quantitative Bound for Complexity 1 Systems)
statement_text: For complexity 1 systems, the dependence of $\delta$ on $\epsilon$ in the definition of complexity 1 satisfies $\delta = \epsilon^{O_A(1)}$, i.e., polynomial dependence.
context_text: Let $\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field and $A$ an $\ell\times k$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_q$. For a finite-dimensional $\mathbb{F}_q$-vector space $V$ and functions $f_1,\dots,f_k:V\to\mathbb{C}$, let $\Lambda_A(f_1,\dots,f_k)$ be the average of $f_1(x_1)\cdots f_k(x_k)$ over all $\mathbf{x}=(x_1,\dots,x_k)\in V^k$ with $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{0}$, and let $\widehat f(\gamma)=\mathbb{E}_{x\in V}f(x)\overline{\gamma(x)}$ be the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at a character $\gamma$ of $V$. The matrix $A$ has complexity 1 if for every $\epsilon>0$ there is $\delta>0$ such that for every $V$ and all $f_1,\dots,f_k:V\to[-1,1]$, $|\Lambda_A(f_1,\dots,f_k)|\le\epsilon$ whenever $\min_i\|\widehat f_i\|_\infty\le\delta$. Examples: any single equation $\sum a_ix_i=0$ with at least three nonzero coefficients, or the cycle relations of a directed graph; a system given by linear forms $L_1,\dots,L_k$ has complexity 1 if and only if $L_1^2,\dots,L_k^2$ are linearly independent (with a technical modification for even $q$), by work of Gowers–Wolf and Hatami–Hatami–Lovett. The authors remark that the general dependence of $\delta$ on $\epsilon$ is a wide open problem, and that conjecturally $\delta=\epsilon^{O_A(1)}$ works (they point to work of Manners for discussion). The paper uses complexity 1 to prove an induced arithmetic removal lemma over finite fields. This is a problem of additive combinatorics.
